body.p: Claims 1-20 will be pending after entry of the present paper. Claims 1 and 10 are amended. Support for the amendments may be found in the originally filed specification, drawings, and claims. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application in view of the amendments and remarks submitted herein.
The Office Action rejects claims 1-5, 9-11, 14-16 and 20 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being

unpatentable over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0164988 to Alvarez ("Alvarez") in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2022/0111087 to Childress ("Childress"). The Office Action rejects claims 6, 7, 12, 17 and 18 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Alvarez in view of Childress and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2018/0369434 to Callahan ("Callahan"). The Office Action rejects claims 8, 13 and 19 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Alvarez in view of Childress and Callahan and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2008/0131332 to Nguyen ("Nguyen"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 1 recites "a central controller coupled to the plurality of touchless sensors, the

actuator; and the light source, the central controller configured to make an inference as to a portion of the lavatory that was used based on the data received from each of the plurality of touchless sensors and to control at least one of the actuator and the light source based on the inference, wherein the central controller is further configured to determine a health status of the system, the health status including a remaining life of the ultraviolet light source, and to control the ultraviolet light source further based on the health status, wherein the health status is based at least in part on the duration of use of the ultraviolet light source." The cited references, either alone or in combination, fail to disclose or contemplate each and every element of amended claim 1.

The Office Action states that Alvarez "does not disclose that the central controller is further configured to determine a health status of the system" and instead turns to Childress. (Office Action, pg. 3.) However, Childress fails to cure the deficiency of Alvarez. Childress states "the control unit 118 ... determines the location of the UV lamp 104 within the area, and control the power, irradiance level, and time of UV light emission output by the one or more UV light emitters 108 based on the determined location of the UV lamp 104." (Childress, [0165], emphasis added.) Childress further clarifies that "when the UV lamp 104 is within a lavatory, the control unit 118 may

operate the one or more UV light emitters 108 at a first power for a first time period" and "when the UV lamp 104 is within a different area, such as a cargo area, galley, flight deck, or the like that may not require the same amount of disinfection, the control unit 118 may operate the UV light emitters 108 at a second power, which may be less than the first power, for a second time period, which may be less than the first time period." (Childress, [0165].) That is, control unit 118 of Childress operates the UV lamp 104 based on the location of the UV lamp 104. In contrast, claim 1 recites "control the multiple light sources further based on the health status." Therefore, Childress fails to disclose or contemplate at least "control the multiple light sources further based on the health status," let alone "the health status is based at least in part on the duration of use of the ultraviolet light source." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 1 be reconsidered and withdrawn.
Claim 10 is amended similar to claim 1 and is therefore patentable for at least the same

reasons as discussed above. Claims 2-9 and 11-20 depend from claims 1 and 10, respectively, and are therefore patentable for at least the same reasons as discussed above, further in view of their own respective features. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1- 20 be reconsidered and withdrawn.

In view of the above remarks and amendments, Applicant respectfully submits that all pending claims are in condition for allowance. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the Examiner's convenience, if doing so will further prosecution of the subject application. The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any fees that may be required or credit any overpayment to Deposit Account No. 192814. This statement does NOT authorize charge of the issue fee.
